title: Dare to Lead: Brave Work. Tough Conversations. Whole Hearts.
author: Brené Brown
target_audience: Anyone interested in vulnerability-based leadership and personal growth
core_themes: Difficult conversations and giving constructive feedback
Fostering innovation and creativity through openness
primary_purpose: To equip aspiring and established leaders with the emotional tools and practical strategies to lead with courage, foster trust, and create more resilient, connected teams and organizations.

structure_format.organization: Organized into four main sections: Rumbling with Vulnerability, Living into Our Values, Braving Trust, and Learning to Rise.
features: Checklists and tools for immediate application

key_concepts_lessons: True leadership requires vulnerability and the willingness to experience uncertainty, risk, and emotional exposure.
Trust is built in the smallest of moments and is foundational for productive teams.
Clear is kind—direct, honest feedback is necessary for growth.
Living into core values guides tough decisions and authentic action.
Learning to ‘rumble’ with difficult conversations leads to stronger relationships and better outcomes.
Developing resilience and self-awareness allows leaders to recover and grow from setbacks.
style_tone: Challenging (asks readers to reflect deeply and confront discomfort)
notable_features: Applies Brené Brown's original research on vulnerability and shame to the context of leadership
Includes actionable tools and exercises for leaders and teams
Blends academic research with accessible storytelling
Focus on 'Wholehearted leadership'—balancing strength and sensitivity
Adapted for organizational training and workshops worldwide
cultural_historical_context: Published in 2018 amidst increased attention to workplace culture, emotional intelligence, and the impact of leadership style on organizational success. The book builds on Brené Brown’s prior bestselling works and her viral TED talks, pushing against traditional, stoic models of leadership.
reception_impact: Became a bestseller and is widely cited in leadership and business development programs
Praised for translating complex psychological concepts into actionable leadership advice
Adopted by Fortune 500 companies, nonprofits, and public sector organizations for leadership training
Critics occasionally note the content may lean towards reiteration of Brown’s previous books, but generally praise its organizational focus and practical tools
comparable_titles: Leaders Eat Last by Simon Sinek
The Five Dysfunctions of a Team by Patrick Lencioni
The Fearless Organization by Amy C. Edmondson
